memories.content: Link expected participant burden in each user study task to its corresponding mitigation strategy.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the prototype and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided during user study sessions.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately after collection.
Specify the equipment to be loaned to participants who lack necessary devices.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
HCI ethics reviewers verify that expected burdens and mitigation strategies correspond to each user study task.
Inform participants that the formative evaluation prototype is not a finished service.
Set an upper limit on cumulative task burden when requesting repeated evaluations from the same participant.
The author of this proposal tends to emphasize expected benefits of the prototype over participant burden.
In organizations where leaders or institutional staff handle recruitment, recruitment authority and academic or professional evaluation authority may be combined in the same role.
Conduct one review prior to submission focusing solely on the validity of user problems, system interventions, and field evaluation logic.
Cross-check whether research questions align with the core functions of the system.
Cross-check whether field tasks align with representative measures.
Cross-check whether the evidence to be collected aligns with the design and operational decisions to be changed.
Finally verify that the user problem, system intervention, field evaluation, and expected contribution form one coherent logical flow.
HCI reviewers view the validity of design interventions as low if research questions do not connect to system functions.
HCI reviewers view the validity of evaluation plans as low if field tasks fail to generate representative measures.
HCI reviewers view the practical utility of contributions as low if collected evidence cannot change design or operational decisions.
Before submission, conduct a sequential walkthrough with field liaisons of installation failures, operational interruptions, and recovery scenarios.
Verify in one sentence how each proposed contribution could actually alter specific design or operational decisions.
The user must distinguish unconfirmed field partners and equipment from finalized ones so remaining execution risks can be assessed.

analysis.overview: The reference frame concentrates on participant protection, access, equipment support, privacy, burden, and recruitment power. The compared frame concentrates on proposal coherence, evaluative validity, decision-relevant evidence, operational walkthroughs, and execution-risk disclosure. These are independently useful policy areas without a direct cross-frame semantic relation.
